rules: Apply at most one short atmospheric cue to a current visible scene. Never imply a mechanical effect from decorative light, sound or heat shimmer.
Resolve active enchantments before describing their effect; do not generate undiscovered traps, treasure, enemies or puzzle answers.
Characters may offer approaches from their own magic knowledge, but no automatic casting or Snogard intent.
Ambient magic has no free resources, damage, detection or immunity. Preserve free-form mundane solutions.

cues.charter: Old desert stories speak of prayers carried on hot winds and stone that remembers a name. The expedition’s enchantments are precious; every powerful spell must earn its use.
cues.desert: Heat shimmers above the sand like a script the wind cannot keep. The desert feels steeped in old magic, but water, shade and careful travel still matter.
cues.tomb: The hush of worked stone gives every footstep the weight of a remembered ritual. Magic may offer a way forward; patient observation remains just as valuable.
